exposure: Antenatal care provider (obstetrician, obstetrician and midwife, midwife)
cohort: The study included 5,143 women aged 15-49 years from urban areas in Indonesia who had recently given birth via cesarean section or vaginal birth.
finding: Women who received antenatal care from an obstetrician had 6.6 times higher odds, and those cared for by an obstetrician and midwife had 2.1 times higher odds, of undergoing a cesarean section compared to women whose antenatal care was provided solely by a midwife.
mod_finding: Antenatal care provided by an obstetrician, or a combination of an obstetrician and midwife, was significantly associated with a higher likelihood of cesarean section.
cross-section timing: Data was obtained from the 2012 Indonesia Demographic and Health Survey.
